sections.heading: produceBlockV4WithBid Endpoint
sections.summary: Luca requested the endpoint be shipped as Experimental; Nico raised trust concerns about untrusted builders; clients asked to review the PR.
sections.body:
- Luca (Vero) posted additional motivation to [beacon-APIs#627](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/627) two weeks ago and received no feedback until this call.
- The endpoint has been tested for over a month on devnet 8; Luca requested it be marked as an Experimental endpoint rather than a production one.
  - Luca updated the PR during the call to add the Experimental tag.
- Nico (Lodestar) raised the main concern: the validator client cannot fully verify a builder's bid, so a single untrusted builder can grief other builders by sending an absurdly high value that the VC cannot reject.
  - With the current Beacon-node-connected builder flow, the BN has full state and fork choice info to reject invalid bids; this protection is lost when bids come through the VC.
  - This pushes the ecosystem toward trusted relays rather than the trustless model aligned with ePBS.
- Potuz (Prysm) argued this is an operator-level trust problem, not a protocol problem, and the BN already trusts external info in many other endpoints.
- Chat discussion explored a possible mitigation: the VC could send a list of bids so the BN picks the first valid one, which would allow untrusted builders to be contacted.
  - Luca noted this could be impractical with many bids (e.g. 100) but acknowledged it could work.
  - Cayman noted sorting and sanity-validating 100 bids shouldn't be a problem for the BN.
- Lighthouse was not present; Eitan said he would talk to Mark, who was reported to be strongly against the endpoint.
- Justin asked clients to review and approve the PR.

sections.heading: Heze-devnet-2 Scope and IL Deadline
sections.summary: Agreement to use existing Beta 4 release for heze-devnet-2 without a new spec release; IL deadline change from consensus-specs#5727 deferred.
sections.body:
- Justin raised whether the inclusion list deadline change from [consensus-specs#5727](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5727) should be included in heze-devnet-2.
- Jihoon confirmed the PR is already merged into the main branch but no new release has been cut, because quick slots discussion was contentious and it was decided not to include quick slots in heze-devnet-2.
- Without a new release and without quick slots, heze-devnet-2 would use Beta 4, which already includes the two CFI'd EIPs (EIP-8365 and EIP-8015).
- Barnabas noted the IL deadline is just a config value and not critical.
- Agreement: no new spec release; heze-devnet-2 uses Beta 4; the IL deadline change is not included in this devnet.

sections.heading: Quick Slots on Heze-devnet-2
sections.summary: No consensus on including quick slots in heze-devnet-2; quick slots spec to remain on a feature branch, not merged into the main Heze spec.
sections.body:
- Potuz asked whether quick slots would be included in heze-devnet-2; Justin argued against, Barnabas argued for.
- Justin's reasons against: would require cutting a new release, complicates testing, makes it harder for clients without quick slots support to join devnet 2.
- Potuz said he didn't mind either way; Lodestar (Matthew Keil) sided with Justin.
- Jihoon offered to create a new PR that places quick slots on a feature branch based on the latest Heze spec, with test vectors clients can pull in.
- Potuz supported the feature-branch approach: clients can pull test vectors into their own feature branches without disrupting production code.
  - Merging into the main branch would force teams to skip code paths in production, which is disruptive.
- Justin stated quick slots should remain a feature branch for at least another month, until after Devcon.
- Barnabas noted that for Glamsterdam (Amsterdam), all small EIPs were merged into the main branch before classification, so the current approach is a change in practice.

sections.heading: CFI/SFI Process and Feature Branch Workflow
sections.summary: Disagreement on whether CFI EIPs must be SFI'd before joining devnets; topic deferred to next ACDC for formal clarification.
sections.body:
- Justin proposed a clearer process: CFI EIPs live on feature branches, are tested on devnets from those branches, and only merge into the main upgrade spec after SFI.
- Francesco noted this creates a circular dependency: previously the expectation was that devnet testing was needed before SFI, but now the suggestion is SFI before joining an official devnet. He asked for the process to be made explicit.
- Potuz disagreed with Francesco's characterization, arguing that devnet testing from feature branches does not require merging into the main spec; ePBS itself was never merged until it was CFI.
- Barnabas countered that all small Glamsterdam EIPs were merged before classification.
- Potuz proposed that the two smaller EIPs already in the main Heze spec (EIP-8365, EIP-8015) should be moved to SFI at the next ACDC call so their status is clear.
  - Justin supported this.
- Jihoon asked whether those two EIPs should be pulled from Heze; Potuz and Justin both said no — they are already passing test vectors and have strong support.
- Decision deferred to the next ACDC call for formal process clarification.
- Chat discussion: a PR at [ethereum/pm#2275](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/2275) proposes that unmerged EIPs stay off call agendas and PFI'd EIPs without client support default to DFI; clients asked to review before ACDE #248.

sections.heading: 0x00 Deposit Handling After Heze Fork
sections.summary: Barnabas proposed making post-fork 0x00 deposits inactive instead of burning ETH; no consensus reached, discussion deferred to next ACDC.
sections.body:
- Barnabas proposed changing the current EIP behavior for post-Heze 0x00 deposits: instead of burning the deposited ETH, the validator would be created as inactive (with a very high activation epoch), recoverable via a BLS-to-execution-change operation.
  - He linked [consensus-specs#5744](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5744) and [EIPs#12513](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12513).
  - Argument: 0x00 deposits are a valid operation today; making a previously valid operation burn ETH after a fork is unacceptable, especially for uninformed operators.
- The current EIP drops 0x00 deposits in the `applyPendingDeposit` function, effectively burning the ETH.
  - NC opened a draft PR ([EIPs#12533](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12533)) to move the guard to `process_deposit_request` instead, which is also simple.
- Potuz noted the current spec is trivial (just drop the deposit) and Barnabas' change is strictly more complicated.
- Justin said both approaches are roughly the same complexity and expressed mild support for Barnabas' change.
- Nico argued for keeping the current simpler spec, noting NC's analysis showed only two 0x00 deposits in the last 6 months; suggested fixing tooling (e.g., launchpad) instead.
- NC raised a concern: Barnabas' approach creates more entities dependent on the BLS-to-execution-change mechanism, which is itself destined for deprecation.
- Barnabas outlined a multi-fork vision: (1) make 0x00 deposits inactive, (2) force-exit remaining 0x00 validators, (3) disable BLS-to-execution-change entirely — by which time a new PQ deposit mechanism would exist.
  - NC cautioned against assuming future EIPs will be CFI'd/SFI'd.
- Discussion on top-ups: the current EIP does not affect top-ups (only new 0x00 deposits). Barnabas and Potuz confirmed that launchpad top-ups currently use zeroed-out withdrawal credentials (0x00), not 0x02.
- Potuz suggested an alternative minimal change: simply never create a validator with 0x00 withdrawal credentials (don't activate, don't burn), but acknowledged this doesn't let users recover funds.
- No consensus reached; Barnabas asked to bring this to the next ACDC call.
  - Justin agreed to discuss at ACDC this week.

sections.heading: Meeting Duration
sections.summary: Agreement to extend ACDT calls to 90 minutes going forward, ending early when there are no remaining topics.
sections.body:
- Potuz and Matthew Keil suggested making the ACDT call 90 minutes, given recent meetings have been very full.
- Justin agreed and said he's happy to moderate longer calls.
- Approach: schedule 90 minutes but end early when topics are exhausted.
